transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

That usually means the door balance spring system has failed or come loose. On built-in Hotpoint dishwashers the door is held by springs, normally linked to the hinges by cords/cables running down each side of the machine. If a cable snaps, slips off, or a spring breaks, the door will suddenly feel heavy and drop open.

Common causes:
• Broken/frayed hinge cord or cable – most likely
• Spring detached or broken
• Hinge damaged
• If the dishwasher has recently had a heavier/lighter cupboard-front fitted, the spring tension may need adjustment — though a sudden change usually indicates a failed cable/spring rather than adjustment.

What to do:
1. Support the door whenever opening it; don’t let it crash down, as it can damage the hinges, front panel, or flooring.
2. Turn off power at the isolator / unplug it before investigating.
3. Check the dishwasher’s rating label (usually around the inside edge of the door) for the full Hotpoint model number.
4. A repairer can usually replace the door hinge cable/spring kit without replacing the whole dishwasher. Often it is sensible to replace both sides together, even if only one has visibly failed.

Avoid trying to tension or remove springs with the machine unsecured — built-in units may need to be pulled out of the cabinet and springs can be under load.

If you give me the model number from the label, and whether the door drops freely all the way or catches/grinds, I can point you toward the likely part and repair approach.
The sticker's partly peeled but I can see it starts LTF. Door drops all the way down with no resistance, though it still closes and latches ok. Heard a twang last week when it went.
